'''Claudio Baiocchi''' (August 20, 1940 – December 14, 2020) was an Italian mathematician. He was a professor at the [[University of Pavia]] and since the 1990s he was a professor of mathematical higher analysis at the [[Sapienza University]].

He worked on partial differential equations and the calculus of variations. In 1971 he applied his mathematical methods to a free boundary problem in the filtration of liquids through porous media with applications in civil engineering (by using the Baiocchi transform).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Baiocchi, C.|title=Sur un problème à frontière libre traduisant le filtrage de liquides à travers des milieux poreux|journal=C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris|volume=273|year=1971|pages=1215–1217}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Baiocchi, C.|title=Sur un problema di frontiera libera connesso a questioni di idraulica|journal=Ann. Mat. Pura Appl.|volume=92|issue=4|year=1972|pages=107–127|doi=10.1007/BF02417940 |s2cid=122863538 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Baiocchi, C.|author2=Comincioli, V.|author3=Magenes, E.|author4=Pozzi, G.A.|title=Free boundary problems in the theory of the fluid through porous media: existence and uniqueness theorems|journal=Ann. Mat. Pura Appl.|volume=96|issue=4|year=1973|pages=1–82|doi=10.1007/BF02414909 |s2cid=119934268 }}</ref>

His later research dealt with, among other topics, the [[Collatz problem]],<ref>{{cite journal|author=Baiocchi, C.|author2=Morgenstern, Maurice|title=Cellular automata about the 3x+1 problem|journal=Proc. LCCS 2001|publisher=University of Paris}}</ref> [[cellular automaton|cellular automata]] and [[Turing machine]]s.<ref>Three small universal Turing machines, in: Machines, computations and universality, LN computer science 2055, Springer 2011, 1–10</ref>

In 1970 Baiocchi received the [[Caccioppoli Prize]]. In 1974 he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Vancouver]]. He was elected to the [[Accademia dei XL]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.accademiaxl.it/it/accademia/soci/soci-nazionali.html |title=Member list of the ''Accademia Nazionale della Scienze detta dei XL'' |access-date=2015-09-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001111436/http://www.accademiaxl.it/it/accademia/soci/soci-nazionali.html |archive-date=2015-10-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Accademia dei Lincei]].
